speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate a potential skin lesion you are concerned about; could you please describe its exact location, size, shape, and how it has changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; given your age, smoking history, and the appearance of non-healing, crusty lesions on both the penis and your finger, we need to rule out squamous cell carcinoma. Please tell me if you have experienced any bleeding, pain, or itching at these specific sites, and have you noticed any changes in the borders or color?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and cutaneous).

Based on your history of smoking, age, and non-healing crusty lesions on the penis and finger that failed prior treatments, this presentation is highly suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma. I need to confirm if there is any associated lymphadenopathy or ulceration before we proceed to a biopsy.
